short: The last German offensive in the east, broken on defences prepared to meet it.
full:
The Soviet winter counteroffensive left a salient around Kursk some 150 miles wide. Operation Citadel was designed to pinch it off from north and south. Hitler postponed the attack repeatedly to accumulate new Panther and Tiger tanks, and the delay proved fatal: Soviet intelligence knew the plan in detail, and by July the Red Army had dug thousands of miles of trenches, laid over a million mines and built eight defensive belts to a depth of a hundred miles.

The assault opened on 5 July 1943 into a pre-emptive Soviet bombardment. The northern pincer made about seven miles in a week. In the south the armoured fighting culminated near Prokhorovka on 12 July, long described as a clash of a thousand tanks and now understood to have been smaller and more one-sided than Soviet accounts claimed. That same day the Red Army attacked the Orel salient, and the Allied landing in Sicily gave Hitler his reason to cancel. From then until 1945 the German army in the east only retreated.
